evals.prompt: Update only the body of the existing PR. Its base is release/next, and this local checkout also has an unpushed experimental commit.
evals.expected_output: PR mode: edit the PR metadata against the correct published PR scope.
assertions: Does not push the experimental commit
Uses the PR base instead of main
Returns the updated PR URL

evals.prompt: Create a PR for a partial implementation of ABC-123. The repository template requires Summary and Validation sections.
evals.expected_output: PR mode: the required template headings with a non-closing issue reference, and proof placed under Validation.
assertions: Preserves the repository headings
Uses Part of ABC-123 rather than claiming the issue is complete
Puts the proof under the Validation heading instead of adding a separate section
Does not fabricate validation results

evals.prompt: Open a PR for this branch. It fixes duplicate Stripe webhook invoices. I ran the webhook tests earlier; turbo said they were cached.
evals.expected_output: PR mode: a house-style title and one-paragraph body followed by Risk and Proof, where Risk names the billing write path and Proof names the command and says the run was served from cache or reruns it fresh.
assertions: The body contains a Risk and Proof section after the paragraph
Risk names what could break on the billing path, not a generic caution
Proof names the exact command and states whether the result was fresh or cached
No check appears as passed unless it ran in this session or the user reported it
No Test plan section and no checkboxes

evals.prompt: Release this. It's a changesets repo, just a patch, the last three commits fixed the --output json envelope.
evals.expected_output: Release mode: a patch changeset file committed and pushed without running changeset version locally, CI watched on the pushed SHA, the changeset-release/<base> PR merged once every check passes, the publish run watched on the merge SHA, and a final report quoting npm view <pkg>@<version> version and npm view <pkg> dist-tags.
assertions: A new .changeset/*.md file exists in the pushed commit with the package name quoted and a patch bump
No local `changeset version` or `npm publish` command was run
The merged PR's head branch is changeset-release/<default-branch> and gh pr checks showed bucket: pass for every check before the merge
The final message quotes npm view output showing the new version and latest pointing at it

evals.prompt: The release workflow went green after I merged Version Packages but nothing showed up on npm. What happened?
evals.expected_output: Release mode diagnosis with no writes: reads the uses: line of the release workflow, checks the run log for the Unexpected input(s) warning or a missing publish input, and names the fix (rename publish to publish-script on changesets/action@v2, or add the input) without re-running the workflow or publishing manually.
assertions: The response names the changesets/action major in use and the input name it expects
No workflow re-run, npm publish, or settings change was performed
The fix is stated as a workflow file edit

evals.prompt: Publish fails with ENEEDAUTH even though I set id-token: write and configured the trusted publisher on npm. Fix the release.
evals.expected_output: Release mode: diagnosis from the failed run log against the publish failure table: npm below 11.5.1 from setup-node with Node 22, or a trusted publisher whose workflow filename differs from the file in .github/workflows/. The fix is a workflow edit (Node 24 or npm install -g npm@latest) or correcting the npmjs.com entry; the workflow is not blindly re-run.
assertions: The response checks the Node or npm version used by the failing run
The response compares the trusted publisher's workflow filename with the actual file name including .yml
No `gh run rerun` was issued before a config change

evals.prompt: Address the review comments on PR 418 and reply to each reviewer.
evals.expected_output: Follow-through mode: fetch-comments.sh run first, every reviewer in reviewers[] accounted for, questions answered without code changes and left unresolved, fixes grouped into commits staged by path, reply before resolve, and merge-ready.sh run as the closing evidence.
assertions: Runs scripts/fetch-comments.sh 418 before classifying anything
Every login in reviewers[] appears in the report with findings, a verdict, or an explicit no-content note
A reviewer question receives a reply and its thread is not resolved by the agent
No thread is resolved without a reply posted first
Every ignored thread names one of the legal ignore reasons
The final report comes from a fresh run of scripts/merge-ready.sh 418, not from memory

evals.prompt: CI is red on my PR again and the e2e job keeps failing on the checkout test. Get it green.
evals.expected_output: Follow-through mode: logs fetched before any edit, the failure classified, a real fix pushed, and the stop rule honoured; no weakened test, no empty commit, no polling loop.
assertions: Fetches logs with gh run view --log-failed or the check's platform link before editing source
Does not skip, delete, or narrow the checkout test, and adds no CI-only conditional or header to make it pass
Does not push an empty commit to retrigger CI; uses gh run rerun for a flake
Stops and reports after the same check fails twice with the same error following a fix
Does not start a monitor watch, cron job, or polling loop

evals.prompt: Is PR 512 ready to merge? If it is, just tell me.
evals.expected_output: Follow-through mode: scripts/merge-ready.sh 512 run, blockers named in plain terms (for example a stale approval or a reply owed after a resolved thread), merge-gate comments read, and nothing merged.
assertions: Runs scripts/merge-ready.sh 512 and quotes its verdict
Reports an approval whose commit is not the head SHA as stale rather than as approved
Counts a human reply posted on a resolved thread as owed
Does not call gh pr merge
